Summary: They are somewhat ok, but I wouldn't get them again.
Text:
Coconut is the dominate flavor and texture in these cereal bars. If you don't like coconut then avoid them. The picture also shows chocolate, which is in there for sure, but it is overpowered by the other flavors.

After reading several reviews, I picked up a package of these at my local Whole Foods (didn't want to buy a 6 pack without trying them first).  I expected a weird texture and taste, but I was pleasantly surprised.  I did a lot of research on preparation, so I ended up rinsing the noodles for a couple of minutes, boiling them for about 5 minutes, and then pan-frying them until there was no more water coming out of them.  I tasted them at this point, and when people say they taste like nothing, they're right on.  The noodles basically taste like water shaped into pasta, which is fine by me because pasta is more of a vehicle for delicious sauce (in my mind).  I mixed these into some homemade alfredo sauce, and I didn't have any issues with texture, taste, or smell.  I actually thought the texture was very very similar to regular, slightly overcooked spaghetti. If I had it my way would they have a bit more of an al-dente texture?  Sure.  But given these have no carbs and no calories, absorb flavor well, make your meal feel more satisfying, and stand up to sauce much better than spaghetti squash, you'll hear no complaints from me!

I love dried cherries and part of the reason for that is that they have a bit of tang to them.  I bought some in bulk before I bought these, and I guess I expected them to be pretty much the same.  They're not.  These are monster mouth-puckering dried cherries.  And trust me, there's no way to tame a tart cherry. I wound up giving them to a friend because they made my mouth cry when I ate them.  But if you like really tart cherries, these are the ones for you!  The resealable bag is great, as long as you remember to squeeze out most of the air before you finish sealing the bag.  The cherries were soft and moist, which is a good thing for a dried cherry; so often they're cherry leather.  And each time I went back to the bag, they were still soft and moist, so the packaging is excellent for nibblers.  But remember, Kirkland has discovered the world's tartest cherries, so if you don't like them that way, don't buy these.  But if you do, run!  The price is great and the bag truly does keep them soft and most.

Summary: Good coffee taste, not too sweet
Text:
The can of illy issimo Coffee Drink claims "100% natural Arabica coffee and the finest ingredients". There are in fact only four ingredients, the first two of which are coffee and sugar. Note - no High Fructose Corn Syrup here. The other two ingredients aren't what you'd typically put in for yourself, potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate, often added to drinks to regulate acidity.

The taste is pretty good for a canned product - nice strong coffee flavor, the way I like it. Perhaps a bit more sugar than I would normally use, but less than I find in most commercial drinks. There is a hint of chemical in the taste, but it isn't obnoxious. I found it quite refreshing. One can is 50 calories, about 2/3 what you'd find in the equivalent amount of soda. Caffeine content is 155mg per can, about on par for brewed coffee and maybe twice what a typical can of an "energy drink" contains.

I must say I drink this coffee all the time. When I found out my local shopping market couldn't keep up with the demand I was heart-broken. When i have to travel an hour and a half to lake george every few months I would stop and buy 9 container but they were small. They would last me 3 days with me and my roommates drinking it. Now I'll buy this and 5 cans from an hour and a half a way and they last me three and sometimes four weeks. I do have a Kerig but I prefer this kind. I cannot strive on how good it taste and how reasonable this is to buy on here.

Whoa...in doing my research I noticed that one box of South Beach Diet Bar Fiber Granola Bar (that's a mouthful isn't it) costs $23.92 if you order it on Amazon. I have prime but I realize that not everyone does so if you factor in another couple bucks for shipping...ridiculous price. I'm not sure how much a box of this costs in stores (considerably less I would hope) but I daresay that it is unlikely that the price is worth the product. If anyone could use a good diet bar it's me but the problem with diet bars is in the name. They are DIET bars. They aren't supposed to taste great (otherwise you'd be in danger of eating the whole box and what kind of diet is that) so instead they usually taste like a mix of cardboard and...well more cardboard. Now the South Beach Diet Bar Granola Bar isn't THAT awful. Don't take that delicious looking beast on the package for truth. The real product is much flatter...And the taste? Well it tastes exactly what you would think a chocolate diet bar would taste like. It's unfair for me to bash a diet bar based on taste after admitting that diet bars aren't SUPPOSED to taste good but that image on the package really got my hopes up.

But how effective is the bar? Effective enough. I ate one this morning and I didn't eat again till later this evening. That's not really praise for the diet bar, I have a pretty hectic schedule. But maybe I didn't notice the hunger as much. I'm guessing I could eat a granola bar (get better taste at a cheaper price) and be the same level as hungry. So if you take diets/diet bars seriously then this might be the bar for you. It doesn't really have anything to separate it from the other snack bars out there other than the South Beach name but hey, what do I know?

Summary: Dogs love them, but I don't think they love dogs
Text:
I will continue to give these to my dogs. They like them and supposedly they clean their teeth.
I started to give these to my dog daily, but her digestive system did not like it enough for that. Most of it seems to be digestible, but she threw up green foam on the morning after the second day in a row of eating one-a-day greenies. Note that she was also constipated as well. Greenie advises to have plenty of water available for drinking these, so I am guess they know these side effects can occur. My dog has plenty of water available, but she didn't drink any more than normal, which may have resulted in the effects. I don't plan on training my dog to drink lots of extra water after eating these. Giving here one every now and then shows no negative effects, and that what I plan on doing.

Summary: We use in Rancilio espresso machine
Text: It is important to know how your coffee is decaffeinated.  For example, one method is the direct method which uses methylene chloride in the process.  Methylene chloride is also used in paint strippers and degreasers.  This chemical was also banned by the FDA for use in  hairsprays and cosmetics, but is still in use for decaffeinating coffee...hmmm.  Now, I am not an expert on the decaffeination process or the justification for the chemicals continued use, but I encourage you to do your own research and decide accordingly!!  This coffee is not only organic but uses a Swiss water process to decafinate.  I use this coffee in my Rancilio espresso machine, and it makes an excellent cup of coffee.  We found that with most decaf coffees, it is harder to get nice crema.  With this stuff, the golden crema flows nicely:).  It has an excellent flavor, but if you are looking for a super strong dark roast, this may be a little light for you.  This is now our go to daily coffee.

Summary: This is really yummy flavored coffee
Text:
If you don't believe me when I tell you that the Cafe Excellence Jazzy Java decaf whole bean coffee is very tasty, I should tell you that I've ordered 6 pounds of the stuff thus far.

For purposes of introduction, I consider myself to know a fair amount about coffee and roasting. I own a small batch roaster and often roast my own green beans. I typically make "Swiss Method" coffee in a Jura superautomatic espresso machine.

Typically, I've avoided the flavored coffees. However, in this case I really enjoy the taste of the various flavors. According to their website, Jazzy Java is Cafe Excellence's signature coffee. It is a blend of butter rum, cinnamon and pecan flavors. I really enjoy it.

The roasting job done on the coffee is worth mentioning as well. It looks to me like a full city roast, roasted to the 2nd crack. It's quite full bodied and fresh, but importantly not overroasted.

I generally prefer either decaf or half-caf and you wouldn't know that this is decaf coffee if you hadn't been told that it was. I've tried Cafe Excellence's non-flavored coffees as well and they are also very good to excellent. However, this blend is special. Highly recommended!

Summary: Hard to give a Clear Review
Text:
and I say that because this product isn't designed for my hair.

My father is Caucasian, my mother is Vietnamese. I have a lot of hair. I wouldn't call it oily, but in the summer it can look that way if left to it's own devices. My hair is a little longer than shoulder length and I have rather heavy bangs.

In the Virginia summer, my ends can FRIZZ. And I dislike it, so when I was given this to try, I thought it would be right up my alley.

As others have mentioned, there are no directions on the jar, but I gave it a shot. Let me say this...it smells wonderful! And I thought I would use it like a leave in hair treatment. Since it is so thick (someone else said almost like shortening, and I would agree with that!) I used just a bit and coated my hair with it.

My hair felt nice as it was drying, but a few hours later it felt heavy, and rather greasy. I didn't like the way it felt,and I jumped in the shower again to wash it out.

The more I looked at it the more I began to think this is not for women with my hair type. While looking online I did indeed find the product, and it is marketed for African American women.

I was very surprised to find that the main ingredient in this is petrolatum. The same stuff in AD ointment. WHY would you to put that on your hair?

As I stated, it is hard for me to give a proper review as it isn't made for my hair type, but I can't imagine anyone wanting to put AD ointment/Vaseline on their hair.

Summary: Delicious Tart and Crispy Chips, A Wholesome Snack
Text:
*****
These apple chips are tart, very crispy, and yummy! They don't have the processed or chemically taste that some dried apples have. They also are not soggy at all--I like my apple chips very crispy! They are 100% certified organic, baked with no added sugar, no preservatives or chemicals, no pesticides or herbicides, gluten free, and made from Washington State apples with five apples in every bag. These are a truly healthy and delicious snack.

These particular chips are only just barely sweet, mostly tart. If you want sweet apple chips, you can buy Fuji apple chips from the same company that are just as crisp and good. I like to mix both together for a sweet-tart combo.

I would also recommend buying these chips in smaller bags (the 2.6 ounce size) unless quite a few people are going to be eating these rather quickly. The reason is that exposure to moisture can render these crispy chips too soft. I like buying them in the smaller bags and then repackaging them in a resealable plastic bag to get rid of all of the extra air. Then I take out only what I plan to eat and quickly reseal the bag. My chips are always crispy this way.

Highly recommended.

Summary: Wonderful, fresh vanilla beans, reasonably priced, from a great vendor
Text:
These beans come in a vacuum-sealed package to preserve freshness, and it works extremely well--all the beans that Beanilla sells are moist and plump with a wonderful texture and scent. There are multiple terrific flavors that you can get from Beanilla, but Tahitian is one that I knew well from buying it in extract form in the past. My Tahitian extract was extremely expensive, and I doled it out little by little and made it last for years. Then I discovered the fun and easy process of do-it-yourself vanilla extract, and a world of gourmet-cooking possibilities has opened up to me. My most frequent use of my vanilla extract is for homemade ice cream using my Vita-Mix. It adds an amazing extra zing to the taste that is just delicious.

I had never made my own vanilla extract before I ordered from Beanilla. Their customer service is superb, and one of their representatives told me by email how to make vanilla extract when I asked, and he also explained why one might want to make his/her own vanilla extract. When you make your own, you can be 100% sure exactly what has gone into the extract, which is not always the case with some types of vanilla extract that you buy pre-made. It is also cheaper and a lot of fun to make your own.

Here is the technique for making vanilla extract spelled out in detail for anyone who has not tried it before, and I have uploaded photos demonstrating these steps:

1. Assemble kitchen scissors, good quality vodka, a clean, dark-glass jar (I save all my empty vitamin jars), a funnel, a spoon, something to label the jar, such as a self-sticking label.
2. Remove the beans from the package. Cut each bean lengthwise in half. Then cut the beans horizontally into pieces small enough to fit in the jar and easily be covered by vodka.
3. Place the bean pieces in the jar.
4. Pour 1/2 cup of vodka into the jar per every 3 beans (for 10 beans, it would be a little over 1-1/2 cup). Then tamp down the beans so that all bean parts are covered by the vodka.
5. Put the lid on the jar and label the jar with this information: what kind of vanilla bean you used, the date, the amount of vodka you used in ounces (or whatever measure you prefer), and the number of beans you used, then place the jar in a cool, dry place like a kitchen cabinet (I put mine with my spices).
6. Every week or so shake the jar.
7. After 8 weeks, the vanilla extract is ready to use.

Every wannabee cook knows that to make an above average culinary creation 3 things are necessary: Talent and creativity, a good recipe, and most important, great ingredients. If those 3 are in place then the results will be nothing short of outstanding every single time.
I have been in love with seafood since a toddler when a mini wave took me up to sea and I was rescued by an aging mermaid. I love all things that come from the sea excepting in sushi form, perhaps some of the sea life in raw form does not agree with my palate. I love making seafood dishes, from soups to main entrees. Soups are my biggest weakness for I use to go to a pier where the seafood would arrive early in the morning hours and right then and there a hot pot with water will be waiting to be filled up with all manners of the daily catch. Mussels, fish heads, shell fish, pieces of fish, oysters, octopus, shrimp, etc etc. These selections would be the leftovers, the ones that did not command a sizable market price, they would end in their own version of the french bouillabaisse, with herbs and spices and the phosphorus of the fish heads, in no time the broth would be bursting with natural flavor right from the ocean. Add some lemon (lime here for the lemon in US is not as pungent), a little home made salsa with onions, chilies and tomatoes, and if you were courageous enough extra heat. By the time you would finish this powerful concoction all the phosphorus of the seafood would command to find the nearest hammock and snore for a couple of hours only to wake up feeling like a million dollars.
Enter Knorr Fish Boullion Mix, 32 Ounce Canister: yes, somewhere in its contents there is some vague taste of fish, but it certainly does not taste natural. It seems to be a little on the smoky side, it definitely has its own particular taste but it is way off from an above average fish stock. I have been using Minor's Clam Base (because is the cheapest in price and imparts a delicious total flavor to dishes) and this time I was caught on the curiosity of purchasing this powder form bouillon. I loved the quantity and the powder form mystified me, what if it works as good as what I had been using? Of course is much more affordable than the clam base I am talking about (that one must be refrigerated and it is semi solid but it does have a truly clam smell) so I bought it and immediately tried it on a seafood chowder cilantro based. A very simple soup that includes hulled barley, onions finely chopped, fresh corn, small diced potatoes and fresh chilies properly sauteed with fresh garlic and olive oil and then blended with the cilantro and a couple of cans of quality diced tomatoes, preferably the ones with a little herbs thrown in. Who am I kidding? The ones they sell at Costco! This soup replaces the hard task of making your own fish stock which requires good fish heads with very clear eyes and all the other ingredients. Too much work for a wannabee cook these days but if done right it is every bit as good as anything you can eat these days. Throw some scallops, different fish, clams (if you can find plump ones), two or three fillets of mahi mahi, large shrimp, etc. But in the end, really, if the broth is good that is all a person would need to enjoy a hot cup or two of fish broth.
This one does not quite reach the levels of goodness I am referring to. It does the job but the final product lacks that essence of the sea, it is a little too processed?

The product description calls the Orangettes "Belgian Vitamin C." Except for the luxury price, I'm sure Belgians must be pretty healthy with these around. They're amazing! The combination of orange peel and chocolate has long been popular, but Leonidas does it very well. The dark chocolate is very rich, not bitter, and completely covers the orange peel (which retains a good flavor and isn't overly sweet). Unlike other chocolatiers who often dip the peel only partially, Leonidas has made certain to put their chocolate center stage by using a generous portion. The result is an addictive treat because the flavors linger on the palate and the Orangettes aren't so sweet as to become cloying.

I don't know if these guys are really going to improve your health, but they will definitely improve your day. In my opinion, they're worth the money as an occasional purchase and certainly worth a one-time try.

Summary: Only organic powdered milk I've found yet
Text:
Our family has decided that it would be wise to store a year's supply of food as a hedge against inflation as well as preparation for food supply disruptions due to natural or man-made disasters. Rather than just toss a bunch of mysterious items in the basement that would get thrown away in 20-30 years, I've been buying bulk grains from my local natural food store and cooking with powdered milk and eggs and such.

The local big-chain natural foods store sells this product in this size package, and I've been buying it there. Organic Valley's website says they make a 25 lb bag, but I've never seen that offered for sale. Amazon's regular price is a tad higher than my local store, but the Subscribe & Save price will save me about 10% off, so I'm signing up.

We are not drinking powdered milk or using it on cereal, but we've had zero taste issues incorporating it into all of our cooking. If anything, the meals I'm making have improved dramatically since I'm making so much from scratch using freshly ground flour, etc.

Coconut oil is a saturated fat. At first glance that alone might make dieters and the health conscious recoil in fear.  Haven't we been told that all saturated fats are artery clogging sludge?  As it turns out, coconut oil is emerging as a near miracle food. Pacific Island populations who get 30-60 percent of their total caloric intake from fully saturated coconut oil have all shown nearly non-existent rates of cardiovascular disease.  The multitude of benefits, including strengthening the immune system and regulating metabolism, make fascinating reading readily available in technical journals and web resources.  Unlike many foods considered healthy, coconut flesh is incredibly delicious.  Since most of us, though, don't relish the idea of hacking the nut to pieces with machetes in the kitchen, coconut is being made conveniently available as in this product, Coconut Manna; a combination of ground coconut flesh and associated oil.  I've been incorporating coconut oil into health shakes so was anxious to try this product which incorporated the flesh as well.  Anyone who has used coconut oil knows that it likes to congeal and form a solid at normal room temperatures and inevitably so in cool locations.  Opening this coconut manna container revealed what resembled a wad of lumpfish stuck to the walls packed in oil.  Not very appetizing.  A metal spoon employed to break it up encountered stubborn resistance.  Submerging the plastic container in warm water would have returned it to an easily workable state, but not something you typically want to do if making a quick health shake or spread.  For that it lost one or maybe one and a half points.  But that's just the natural state of the food and Nutra can't be faulted for that.  The product itself once more malleable is absolutely delicious.  It's tempting to just eat it off the spoon before it makes it to whatever vehicle you planned to park it on.  For smoothy/shake makers, the pure oil form is probably easier to use, though it can congeal also, though probably not as readily or as stubbornly as this manna. It is delicious, but only if you want to take the time to render it at a temperature to make it more easily spread and applied.

Summary: Not that different from regular shirataki noodles, and they are much cheaper elsewheres
Text:
These House Foods tofu shirataki noodles have only a small amount of soy flour in them - the konnyaku yam flour is still the main ingredient.

I couldn't tell much of a difference between these tofu shirataki noodles and regular shirataki noodles - they may be just a bit softer, but not much.

Shirataki noodles are not a hydrated starch paste like wheat noodles - instead they have the structure of a firm gel and are 96% water with only a tiny amount of the konnyaku yam flour (a long chain polysaccharide) holding it all together.

The gel structure accounts for the mouth feel and chewing texture of the shirataki noodles. This is also what makes them so filling without getting you all those calories. The water soluble fiber of the yam flour is also not digested for the most part, and is very healthy for you.

They do go great with a lot of different stuff - udon soup, tomato or pesto based spaghettis, etc. I give five stars for the shirataki noodles.

The main problem with the House Foods noodles listed here is their price, especially the exorbitant shipping charges. House Foods is actually located in Southern California, and the listed seller is in New York!

There are cheaper suppliers elsewhere.

Text:
I ordered CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm, 6.7 Fluid Ounce not realizing, along with many other consumers, that this works for "ethnic" or "natural" (read: coarse) hair.

... and there are no instructions on the packaging.

I came to Amazon to read other reviews, and saw that the lack of instructions annoyed many other consumers. Ultimately, I gleaned from all the reviews, and I think it worked out OK.

I shampooed and rinsed my hair, and wrung out a lot of the extra watter. I ran my fingers over the top of the CLEAR Nourishing Balm, rubbed my fingers together, combed them through my hair, and repeated. I am used to being very stingy with Jonathan Product Dirt Texturizing Paste(R) 3.35 oz, so this wasn't much of a stretch. All in all, I don't think I used a quarter of a teaspoon.

After about five minutes, I rinsed. It took more doin' to get out the product than regular conditioner would take. I'd hoped it would be as easy as when I used to use another "ethnic" product, Queen Helene Cholesterol Cream, but this was far waxier. I did ultimately get it out.

I followed with a little Paul Mitchell Super Skinny Serum because it was starting to frizz, and went for a haircut.

My hairdresser was less bothered by the waxy finish to my hair than I was, and he saw more "curl pattern" in the back than I could.

No one's running fingers through my hair so the waxy feel doesn't much matter, and the overall appearance (with the Paul Mitchell product) and smell are pleasing. No surprising additional breakage. I had hoped that it would cause less frizz, but maybe I need to use it on a more regular basis. (I've been using it for four days.) I bought this,

an Omega J8006 juicer ( here on Amazon: http://www.amazon.com/Omega-J8006-Nutrition-Commercial-Masticating/dp/B001L7OIVI/ref=sr_1_cc_1?s=aps&ie=UTF8&qid=1328216581&sr=1-1-catcorr ),

a growing rack (here on Amazon: http://www.amazon.com/Gardman-R687-4-Tier-Mini-Greenhouse/dp/B000NCTGQE/ref=sr_1_7?s=home-garden&ie=UTF8&qid=1328216609&sr=1-7 ),

some trays (here on Amazon: http://www.amazon.com/Gardman-R687-4-Tier-Mini-Greenhouse/dp/B000NCTGQE/ref=sr_1_7?s=home-garden&ie=UTF8&qid=1328216609&sr=1-7
and here http://www.amazon.com/Durable-Plastic-Wheatgrass-Growing-Without/dp/B000E7MTUI/ref=sr_1_2?s=home-garden&ie=UTF8&qid=1328216637&sr=1-2 ),

some sprouting soil (bought at my local hydroponic shop, but anything with a high perlite percentage works),

and Azomite (here on Amazon: http://www.amazon.com/Lbs-Azomite-Additive-Fertilizer-Minerals/dp/B000E7MTT4/ref=pd_bxgy_hg_text_b )

The only advice I can give is do NOT overwater. It's easy to do, and you will probably find yourself overwatering that first batch as you get used to growing your own.

This particular wheat sprouts really nicely! I don't see any wasted grains (amazing) and the plants are strong and healthy. The price is right, too, especially with the Prime shipping.

Summary: Inexpensive food; Dog might like it, but not necessarily healthy
Text:
My dog likes this food. The food has a good variety of colors, shapes, and ingredients - beef, grains, and vegetables.

It's actually pretty healthy and has a balanced overall nutrition.

However, the one glaring flaw is the by product. True, this dog food does have a grains, vegetables and beef. But, by product is still part of the ingredients. It's quite unsettling not knowing exactly what is going into the food. By product could be cow feet, butt, skin, anything that is part of a cow but isn't truly meat.

Purina can legitimately claim this to be a natural, whole product.The majority of it does have good ingredients. But as we take a closer look, there is still by-product. I wished it wasn't there, but that would likely increase the price.

I wouldn't necessarily say this dog food isn't good for your dog, but there are better options. If you don't mind the extra ingredients that may not wholesome, this food is fine. It shouldn't be life-threatening nor fatal. I recommend going completely (or at least more so) wholesome and natural with brands like Blue Buffalo and Nutro.

Summary: My Dogs LOVE the Flavor - And It Works
Text:
I have a 7 year-old Border Collie mix, Abbey, who has arthritic knees. She had bilateral arthroscopic knee surgery about a year and a half ago to remove broken bone fragments in her joints. Our vet instructed me to give her an oral glucosamine supplement for the rest of her life. Abbey also gets a glucosamine injection, Adequan, every other week. My vet allows me to administer it myself (at home) to save on vet bills.

The injection turned out to be the simple part. Abbey hated the glucosamine supplement we got from our vet. I had to wrap it in cheese or something, and she usually spit it out once or twice before it went down. She tends to be a little overweight, so the added calories from cheese and other disguises were a negative. I tried several different brands of glucosamine tablets, and she refused every one.

A couple of months ago, my local Petco had a close-out sale on Healthy Motion, so I thought we'd give it try. I opened it and immediately noticed the spicy scent. It smells kind of like Indian food spices. To my great surprise, Abbey and two other dogs came looking before I opened their wet food. It turns out that three of my four dogs PREFER the Healthy Motion-sprinkled food to their otherwise identical wet & dry mixed dinner.

It works! After using it for 2-3 weeks, I noticed that Abbey has more energy and is moving better. Finally, something that is both effective and palatable to her. She looks forward to it and licks up every speck.

Offhand though, I'd rather spend 8 to 12 dollars on a bag of the stuff at my bookstore job & drink that instead. Before buying bulk amounts of this coffee I'd recommend that any potential buyers purchase a bag at their local stores first. Summary: Ok but the CHERRY is better
Text: This "grape" taste is ok - just OK or acceptable, or "will do in a pinch if I have to sacrifice some taste because I want no calories." The cherry flavor, however, is the bomb.

I just don't understand why a product such as this even exists. If I wanted a soda, I would drink a soda. If I wanted to drink fruit juice, I would drink fruit juice. Both have their own merits and qualities. This product just seems to fall "flat" when compared to either soda or juice.

The high amount of carbohydrates and ridiculous amount of sugar makes it just as bad as soda or fruit juice, from the standpoint of raising one's blood sugar levels and causing obesity. Diabetics will want to avoid it altogether. How much protein does it contain? Zero.

As has been noted by other reviewers, the carbonation is definitely much less than with most sodas, which gives it a bit of a "flat" taste. Speaking of taste, it didn't really taste much at all like black cherry. Take one look at the ingredient list, and you'll see why. It's mostly apple and grape juice, which is MUCH cheaper for the company to buy than using real, black cherry flavoring, which there is barely a hint of.

Those of you thinking that there is enough real juice in this beverage to give the listed 100% RDA of Vitamin C are in for a surprise. The only reason that this beverage is able to make the 100% RDA claim is because it separately adds ascorbic acid as an ingredient. In other words, they sprinkle in some powdered Vitamin C in order to make it healthier. If you drank an 8 ounce glass of water, along with a Vitamin C tablet, you would get the same amount of nutrition, while avoiding the extra calories and sugar.

The taste is just "o.k.", at best. Altogether, it isn't necessarily "bad" for you, but there are certainly much healthier things for one to drink. What I really find difficult to understand it why this product is so darned expensive. If you're going to spend that much money, you might as well just buy real fruit juice. I wouldn't buy this product unless it was at least 75% less expensive than it is now.

If you've tried Japanese seaweed snacks and didn't like them, you may like Korean ones. Korean seaweed snacks are typically roasted and flavored with salt and oil while Japanese ones are oil-less. This makes Korean seaweed sheets very light, flaky, and crispy. They just crumble in your mouth. Both are very nutritious and healthy, but Japanese seaweed strips are thicker and more chewy. The downside to the yumminess is that Korean seaweed snacks typically taste saltier, so it's best to eat them with a bowl of rice, though I've gone through several packs of them on their own. Summary: Now my working day Thermos Coffee
Text:
Generally I drink only home pressed espresso - and way too much of it - so for the past few months have been going with drip brewed coffee (except on weekends!) in an effort to cut down on the amount of caffeine I drink.

This works, as I can make drip coffee weaker than espresso without it being too watery, whereas weak espresso is simply dreadful. Recall that "Caffè Americano" is espresso with hot water added to it to make it weak enough for our usual national preference, and is not the sort of coffee that I enjoy.

Perhaps because it is so finely ground, I find myself using under half as much of this Melitta "Blanc et Noir" coffee as I had been using with my previous home ground mix for my drip brewer and still ending up with OK coffee.

The "Blanc et Noir" also seems to be quite "smooth," though I do find myself adding about a third of a teaspoon of sugar per pint else it is slightly bitter - which seems characteristic of all pre-ground coffees.

Though I did get a complementary bag of this coffee from Amazon for review (which is how I found out about it), I liked it well enough that I now have it as a regular order on my Amazon "Subscribe and Save" program.

It is not great coffee, but it is good coffee. It is what I now take to work everyday for it is much better than that which I can get at the hospital, and, as am using less coffee to make it, it not only has further decreased my caffeine intake, but is cheaper as well.

Summary: Usual Starbucks quality delivers the goods
Text:
Starbucks Natural Fusions Vanilla Flavored Ground Coffee combines the usual Starbucks richness and "ooomph" with a subtle vanilla flavor, resulting in a more relaxing, down-to-earth coffee than non-flavored Starbucks varieties. Or to put it another way, it's an enjoyable coffee for those times when you favor a comforting coffee experience over an eye-opening one.

Through Amazon's Vine Program, I also recently tried Melitta Cafe Collection Parisian Vanilla Ground Coffee, and liked that a lot, too. That one was more like a regular cup of coffee, though, less strong and complex than the Starbucks variety described here, though the vanilla flavoring had about the same flavor and strength in both coffees.

It's all a matter of personal taste. Some people like a no-nonsense coffee like the Melitta and some like the gourmet richness of a Starbucks. Myself, I go back and forth. And when I'm in the latter mood, and also in the mood for a flavored coffee, I wouldn't hesitate to pick up this quality Starbucks offering.

Summary: Pretty good, but the new Chocofudge is better
Text: Chips Ahoy! is probably the best-selling chocolate chip cookie in the United States, and I have always thought it was one of the worst.  I've never been a fan of hard chocolate chip cookies and Chips Ahoy! was always the cookie of last resort for me.  Now, though, Chips Ahoy! has launched two new soft chocolate chip cookies:  the one under review here (Megafudge) and Chocofudge.  I think they are both pretty good, but I think the Chocofudge is better.  The Megafudge, as the name implies, is basically white and dark chocolate chips in a chocolate fudge cookie.  It's not bad, but a little too much chocolate for my taste.  So, if you are thinking of trying one of these Chips Ahoy! cookies, you shouldn't be too disappointed with either one, but I would go with the Chocofudge.  Actually, of the mass produced chocolate chip cookies, I like the Pepperidge Farms soft baked Nantucket chocolate chip cookie best.

I did some research on the health benefits of some of these ingredients. This info is what I found reported in a few different sources:

Rooibus tea:
Rooibus tea is rich in antioxidants and flavonoids and is reported to have 50 times more antioxidant power than green tea. It also has other antioxidants not found in other teas. The effect of free radicals in the process of aging and declining of the immune system is limited by the antioxidants in Rooibus tea. Rooibus tea is completely pure and natural . It contains no additives, preservatives or colorant. It is strongly recommended for those suffering from irritability, headaches, disturbed sleeping patterns, insomnia, nervous tension, mild depression or hypertension. It has no caffeine and so has a soothing effect on the central nervous system. Rooibus tea is low in tannin and so it does not have a negative effect on the absorption of iron and proteins into the body. It has anti-spasmodic properties, thus relieving stomach cramps and colic in infants. It also relieves stomach and indigestive problems like nausea, vomiting, hearrtburn, stomach ulcers and constipation. It supplements the daily amounts of calcium, manganese and flouride, and it contains zinc and alpha-hydroxy acid. I was also told that red tea does not have ECOG, a healthful property that green tea does have. That is why I drink both red tea and green tea, to get the best of all worlds.

Rosehips is supposed to be good for infections, bladder problems, and diarrhea and also a good source of vitamin C.
Hibiscus flowers is supposed to be a diuretic (fluid release) and reported to help lower high blood pressure in people with Type 2 diabetes.

If I had only two words to describe the taste of this tea, they would be fruity and smooth. It is also caffeine free. It is a nice change of pace from standard flavors and a nice after-dinner comfort drink. Stash makes a good full bodied tea, stronger than some of these cheapie teas, so I find I only need one bag per a 24 oz cup. (Of course, that all depends on your preference.) These special Stash flavors are a little hard to find because many stores do not carry them unless they have a super large tea display.

BTW--I am not a doctor--(my disclaimer)--just someone who has done a lot of reading on alternative health care. As with any product, consult your health cae provider, especially if you are on medications.

The temptation with a mallomar is to critique the one as three, the cookie and then the marshmallow and then the chocolate, as if three cookies stepped out of a bar together, and were in fact Larry, Curly, Moe, rather than the three stooges of cookiedom.

To see the mallomar as parts, not a whole, as separable, like the Oreo, as split into segments, is to diminish the mallomar. This is philosophical reductionism, the sort of analysis that leads a sloppy thinker to believe that a material element explains the spiritual, that science explains experience, that what a man thinks encompasses what a man does.

The mallomar stands athwart these modernistic tendencies with a traditional meld of flavors, a completeness.

The headline of this review was written during a weak moment, a moment when a nibble was made, the edge tasted, and the chocolate found exceptional. This shallow and specious moment, I preserve in the headline, to show that fateful reduction in essay form is a failing, unlike in the making of a sauce, where reduction is a tool.

Mallomars cannot be reduced. They are one, and the best way to eat one is to take a larger bite, to get marshmallow, cookie, and chocolate in a grasp and a gasp of flavor.

Long live mallomars!. As a midwestern person, I often cannot find them in my grocer, and this is a shame. A shame.

Summary: Good for Asian-style food, but pricey per serving
Text:
I bought 3 pasta shape varieties of these 8 oz. 2-serving bags of noodles in liquid in the refrigerated tofu section of our local grocery store for $1.99 per bag yesterday. I am puzzled how they can be sold and shipped since the front of the bag states "perishable - keep refrigerated". I opened the bag and smelled the noodles, and they did have a rather strange, strong odor. I immediate poured the noodles into a strainer and then rinsed them under cold water. I put them in a sauce pan with a small amount of Lorivo expeller-pressed peanut oil and let them sit for a while, stirring occasionally. I decided to add Guilin chili sauce, garlic powder, powdered ginger, a small amount rice vinegar, water, 3 - 4 tsp. coconut sap sugar and 1/2 large can drained bean sprouts. I warmed this mixture for awhile - maybe 20 or more minutes. It worked! I created a palatable side dish with a good- tasting broth and appealing consistency.

I served this side dish with broiled tuna, mahi mahi, and a Spring greens salad mix with balsamic vinegar and olive oil.
I wish that these noodles were available in larger sized bags at a lower price per serving, but $1 per person for two modest serving sizes per bag isn't outrageous unless you compare this with the cost of regular pasta. I added the bean sprouts because the noodles alone didn't look like enough food for 3 people, and I thought that adding bean sprouts would offset any texture issues with the noodles. This recipe has now worked out twice with no real concern about cooking time for the noodles. Maybe the vinegar is the key, but the noodles are just like any other noodles when prepared this way and they make a great noodles with Asian-style broth meal or side dish. And finally ... a use for those canned bean sprouts!

Update: I have now mixed these with baked tofu and Asian-style sauce. That combo worked out great. Also I took the wide noodles, rinsed them and then put them in spaghetti sauce to simmer. They tasted fine. Texture-wise, they will always be somewhat slimy and slippery and not al dente like well-prepared pasta, but otherwise, they worked out well. Just remember - just 40 calories - in an entire bag! And next to no carbohydrates!

Summary: Best Natural and Quick Flea Control
Text: An odd spin on this product is that it rapidly de-fleas an infested home (or apartment), with ongoing maintenance of combing pets for fleas, etc. I researched everything out there and found one small lone reference to silica as a solution. I also learned that fleas reproduce in stool (thus, the litter box). An infestation that rapidly progressed in my daughter's family home was finally cleared, in a very short time, with improvement (my infant grandson's bites) noted overnight, after adding this to the cat box (along with regular litter) and sprinkled around the home in corners, where walls met carpet, and any place that could be "damp" and a breeding ground. In the sprinkling, we were generous and left it there. It has to be silica (in this case, gel), though. The round litter product (sand) does not work. The initial recommendation I found mentioned products available through hardware stores that I was unable to locally find and were very expensive and large purchases online. The base was silica, which is why this product did the trick. We keep the boxes sprinkled each week as a precaution.

This review is about the tree that I ordered. This Fukien Tea Tree started to loose all of its leaves and appeared to be in distress. I kept it watered, gave it great morning and afternoon light and maintained the temp around 75 degrees. After several weeks, the tree has lost almost all of its green growth. I had an expert view the tree and this gentleman seemed to think that the soil that the tree was planted in was too dense and didn't allow for any oxygen to reach the roots. This enables the pasta to remain al dente.

Heating these dishes is very fast and easy as well. Just peel back a corner of the cover to vent the sauce and pop the dish in the microwave for sixty seconds.

I'm also impressed to see that at Amazon's prices, these dishes aren't horribly exorbitant either. More expensive than Chef Boyardee in a can, but probably a bit less than a frozen entree.

My only quibble is I really wouldn't call one of these dishes a "meal." The portion size is nominally 9 ounces, but I would consider this a light lunch at best -- and I would probably be starving by tea time.

Nevertheless for pasta fans looking for a quick and delicious pasta fix, these Barilla dishes are definitely worth trying.

Years ago a ham radio guy asked me (over the air!) whether I knew how to make gourmet microwave hot cereal. I said no - wondering how you could make anything gourmet, especially cooked cereal, in the microwave - but that I didn't express out loud... so he explained to me the above method, with emphasis on heating the cold water before adding the cereal. I do find myself urinating more often so maybe it is cleaning me out.  No bad side effects, tastes good alone, no sugar or honey needed.  I recommended this to my family and co workers and they all love it.  I discovered this from Dr. Oz.  Hoping to continue to sleep well.

I am from the Midwest and lived in the South for 21 yrs, moved back to the Midwest. I fell in love with this product and cannot live without it in my life. No other mayo is the same. I have it shipped to my house since I am unable to find it here. Love it!

I use this pickled ginger to go along with my nori rolls. The taste is exceptionally fantastic--seriously the best I have had. Organic is a huge plus, and I will continue to purchase/stock up on this. I do think that this is a product that I will begin to use more and more, simply because of its quality. The taste is more mild and pleasant than typical pickled ginger that you receive with sushi. It has a refreshing bite to it, not a weird chemical-biting aftertaste like what most everyone is used to. If you are looking for ginger for your sushi, you will not regret trying a bottle of this!

Ordered on May 23 with super saver shipping and received it on June 22. Was it worth the 30+ day wait? Of course!

$32.66 for 24 boxes = $1.36/box

The price is great, especially for online since you CANNOT find this in stores anymore. I live in a huge city and cannot find this in Target or any supermarkets. The Kraft product locator on the Kraft website was incorrect about it being stocked in stores in my area. AMAZON to the rescue, as usual. It seems this delicacy is nearly extinct which is sad because it's the only Kraft macaroni worthy of your taste-buds.

All the other Kraft mac & cheese makes me think of being an indiscriminate kid that will eat any funny tube-style pasta with bright orange manufactured cheese; perhaps kids 'are' the target market. Yes, THREE CHEESE is Kraft macaroni in a box, but it's amazing. The cheese just tastes good, not heavy or fake, and the shells are perfect size. Add some oregano, red pepper, or even sausage and you've got yourself a tasty yet inexpensive meal.

Milk and butter sold separately.

After trying multiple formulas, we finally found a formula that my son tolerates (doesn't spit up!) A doctor had said that he was suffering from mild reflux which I didn't fully believe and we tried a rice formula and he would spit almost half of it back up. Trusting my instinct I decided to research organic formulas and found Earth's Best. You do need to mix it with warm water in order for it to fully dissolve and shake well - you don't get a lot of excess foam with the shaking. I haven't had any issues with it at all. Now that he's been eating solids, I cook his food but buy Earth's Best jarred food for hard to find fruits and veggies.

Summary: Decent Balsamic. But not the thick syrup stuff
Text: I was trying to find the thick, syrupy stuff I bought a O and Co. The kind that drips out as thick as molasses. This isn't that stuff. Having said that, it's still pretty good. Would be great in salad dressing and price is decent. So it's not bad for what it is, but if you want the best of the best, molasses thick aged stuff, got to look elsewhere.

Summary: Perfect substitute for wide rice noodles!
Text:
These are a perfect substitute for wide rice noodles; I made a stir fry tonight and it was delicious! These noodles hold up much better than rice noodles - don't break and don't get soggy. Also I don't have to obsessively time these since they are cooked and really only need blanching to warm them through (it usually takes about 30 min to soak rice noodles and it's easy to overdo it; not a problem with these).

I WOULD NOT use them in a "pasta" recipe like carbonara, marinara, etc. 'Cause you wouldn't use rice noodles in those recipes, that's why! Personally, I think it's a mistake that the company is labeling these as "Fettucini". This sets up a wrong expectation. They should label these as "wide noodles".

This is delicious, but I wish they would use Stevia instead of NutraSweet. I used half water and half milk instead of 4 cups of skim milk and mixed in a blender instead of mixer (add milk first). After 1 to 2 hours in the refrigerator it was set and ready to eat.

It works well as a pudding if you don't have (or don't want) a crust.

After the last review, I was a little concerned that I wouldn't like it. I suppose, if you like your pumpkin pie really sweet, you'll be disappointed. I like the taste of the pumpkin more than a sweet taste so I was very pleased.

When I was stationed in Germany I started buying this tea and was crazy about it, in fact I made sure I would have plenty to drink once I returned from the states.  When I ran out I started trying to drink the other teas I grew up with, and found those too weak and started ordering PG Tips from Amazon.  One bag of this is about two regular tea bags.
i have been drinking this tea for years and it is the least bitter green tea I have ever tried.  There are 50 bags in a box instead of the usual 24 other teas supply.  Excellent value for the money.

I eat 3 whole tubs of these every day. I think I have a problem. I think I might die soon. You see, my parents were mauled by wild bears when I was a child. So I eat as many gummy bears as I am physically capable of to take revenge upon bears of all kind

Summary: Surprised that my cats don't like these
Text: When I buy a 5 star item from Amazon, it is always a good product. In this case, the product may be just fine quality wise, but for some reason my cats hate these flakes. Of the two cats, when presented with the flakes - one gave me a "are you stupid" look and the other one gave me a "why did you do this to me" look. Both of the cats like all other cat treats and are not picky eaters. Don't know why they don't like these, both of them go nuts for seafood. Given that all the other reviews are very positive, perhaps I got a bad batch of flakes and it is just an aberration, but both cats are very much "Do Not Want!" on these flakes.

Children who can consume sweets by the pound will gladly go through a box of these with no issue. My friend, an adult male who occasionally feels the need to snack - took about two days to consume the box of these. These had the appearance of a smaller, thicker chips-ahoy chewy cookies.

I personally didn't care for them, they were smaller than normal chips ahoy cookies, and seemed damp. The fudgy center didn't really seem fudgy at all but rather made the cookie seem more cakey. The sweetness however was really kicked up a notch - they were so sweet it was almost painful. Although this cookie seemed like a great idea, I'll stick with the chips-ahoy chewy cookies personally. These were too sweet for me and the dampness was just sort of strange and a bit unnerving.

From a kid's perspective these are probably the greatest cookies available in a store (everyone knows that mom's and Grandma's cookies are the best). But the majority of adults would probably prefer the original or chewy cookies.

Stash Chamomile Herbal Tea is tea bags with dried, crushed chamomile flowers.

Honestly, as far as I'm concerned, chamomile is chamomile. I suppose that when you use loose flowers you get sediment in the cup and I have seen this happen with some brands of chamomile tea bags, these don't do that.

I have also had organic chamomile (this isn't) but I can't taste the difference.

Each bag is individually packaged and that is either good or bad depending on how and where you use it and if you are concerned about excessive packaging.

If you like chamomile tea, this is a good choice.

Summary: Our favorite Dolce Gusto flavor so far
Text:
My wife and I just recently purchased the Dolce Gusto machine and we were very curious about the cappuccino flavor. Since I grew up in Germany, I am very familiar with a typical european cappuccino taste and I had high expectations.
I think Dolce Gusto hit this one out of the park. With a little addition of sugar and experimentation of the milk to coffee ratio this capsule can make a delicious cup of cappuccino in about 30 seconds. We are very pleased and can't wait for our free Mocha capsules.

I love this stuff. I ran the New Years Eve Emerald 4 mile run in NYC this year, and I got a free bag of the smores mix. I've been addicted to it ever since.
some stores refuse to carry it, and it's their lose.
best tasting trail mix I ever had..
MM

I have been giving my old golden retriever Happy Hips items for a few years now to help with his arthritis.  He loves these treats along with other Happy Hips items.  These are a great snack for him that I carry in my pocket when we go for walks.  I do think the glucosamine in these has made a big difference in his aching old legs and has helped him stay with me as long as he has.  Thanks for a good product.
I expected more from Kirkland because every other product of theirs is great. These, though, are rather mediocre. I was disappointed.

Summary: 425F seems too high a recommended baking temp
Text: The muffins themselves are quite tasty and easy to prepare, but they probably would have come out much tastier had the edges NOT come out just under burned. :(  Box directions recommend to bake these at 425F for 15-20 min. That seemed pretty extreme to me, especially for Lemon Poppyseed muffins which seem delicate. I baked at 425 but pulled them out after just 12 minutes. Didn't make a difference - they were already nearly black around the edges and on the bottoms by then. Had to eat around the burnt parts. No doubt the whole batch would have been ruined if I'd left them in the recommended 15, and certainly 20 min. Glad I wasn't serving these up to company.

Summary: My favorite tea--I keep coming back to it
Text:
I take strong exception to another reviewer who was disappointed in the taste of this jasmine white tea. I am a long-time tea drinker, and one by one, my "most favorite" teas have fallen by the wayside. The one tea that I can drink day after day and never get tired of it, is this one. Sure, I still drink others just for variety, but this is the one that I always come back to.

I used to buy it at World Market, just like the other reviewer, but my local WM stopped carrying the white teas. I asked an employee there if they would ever have any back in stock, and she said, "Oh the jasmine tea? That's SO GOOD!" But--no, they are no longer carrying it.

The jasmine flavor is not strong, and complements the delicate white tea flavor very well. Like the other reviewer, I use filtered water, but I certainly do not make my own tea bags! Good grief.... And where the reviewer came up with the unwelcome orange smell is beyond me.

I wish Republic of Teas would make a sampler pack of their white teas--then people could try them without shelling out a lot of money.

This is one of my favorite Gelatins. Add bananas and walnuts and it's really good.
Hard to find in local stores, I had to ask my grocer to order a case of 24 in order to get it.
Was worth it!!!

This pancake mix is the best gluten-free equivalent to glutonous Bisquick I have yet seen, but it tastes even better. Though not high in vitamins, it makes wonderful pancakes, banana nut bread, and zuccini bread,

Summary: Tasty and free of nasty fake sugars
Text:
This gum is old school. It doesn't believe in all those fancy, new fangled sugar alternatives. Ingredients are simple: cane sugar, glucose, gum base, rice syrup, beeswax, carnuba wax and flavors. It also doesn't mess around with synthetic color agents (no Red #40 or Yellow #5 lurking in these boxes). Bonus is that it tastes great. No it doesn't stay flavorful for an extra, extra, extra long time, but its delicious for long enough to get a nice minty taste in my mouth and satisfy my desire to chew.

I had discovered Glee Gum years ago and enjoyed it, but hadn't thought much about it again until I became pregnant last year and realized EVER gum at the corner store or gas station had either aspartame or saccharine in it. Even the tried and true Juicy Fruit has turned to the dark side. Thank you Glee Gum for offering this delicious, all natural alternative to the neuro-toxin laced sticks sold by your competitors. I appreciate it and I will continue to buy your fine product for many years to come.
I am so glad I found these! They taste so good & are so convenient plus a fraction of what they would cost individually in stores. Will definitely get again when my supply is running low!

this very fragrant olive oil adds depth to recipes and melds especially well with the summer bounty of tomatoes and basil.  It is also great with any Mediterrean, Provencal, or Italian recipes.  Althought a bit pricey, its flavor and versatility make it worth the cost for cooking with quality ingredients.  It is  probably my favorite olive oil.

My vet thinks my dogs teeth are in great shape and probably never need to be cleaned.  I get the Dentastixs in large and small size.  I like getting the good this way because it is less expensive, I buy enough for free shipping and my dogs LOVE them.  Thank you Amazon

I ate it as dry cereal and it was delicious. I don't know if the almonds are supposed to have bitter/tart taste but it was a bit bitter.
Also, I felt like the portion/size was really small for the price.

UPDATE: These flowers lasted a full two months - every single bud opened, and she got to enjoy them for a long time. Excellent purchase!

I ordered these for my mother, and she thought they were incredibly striking and beautiful, so it's a win!
The order did take a day or two longer than i expected, but the blooms are supposed to last quite a long time.

This is a delightful English candybar. It's not like anything we have in the states. I lived in England for a short time and was able to try quite a bit of different sweets. I am not a fan of British Cadbury chocolate, however, this is the one and only exception for me! It is worth a try for someone wanting to try something new.

Summary: CHOCOLATE CHIPS & FUDGE - WHO COULD ASK FOR MORE?
Text:
CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE COOKIES

We love cookies and were excited to received these. They are chock full of chocolate chips, extremely soft, definitely chewy, and for an added treat, there is a filling of chocolate fudge. The only down side regarding these cookies are perhaps they are a little too soft -- when taking them out of the package to enjoy many of them simply fell apart in my hand.

The packaging is attractive and eye-catching and has the new lift-end resealable package. I find this type of packaging an easy opener, but always find the package does not stay sealed well and end up placing all the cookies in a plastic container or placing the entire package of cookies in a food storage bag to keep fresh.

These cookies are good -- I don't think Chips Ahoy! ever disappoints. However, they are not my favorite Chips Ahoy! cookie, [that would be the regular old plain chocoloate chip non-chewy, thank you] but they are worth every bite and every calorie. For those of you watching calories, fat, sodium, etc -- you may enjoy two cookies for a total of 150 calories, total fat is seven grams, zero cholesterol, and sodium clocks in at 110mg. There is no trans fat involved. So you should definitely have more than two cookies -- go for it!

If you like chocolate chip cookies and fudge, these cookies make for a nice combo. They are delicious with a hot cup of coffee or tea or a tall ice cold glass of milk. Dunking in milk was a bit sloppy since the cookies are so soft, yet still highly recommended.

All in all, not a bad cookie.

Thank you.

Pam

This is my absolute favorite peanut butter of all time. I can't find it in our town, so was happy to see it here. Ordering and shipping, no problem.  The only thing I didn't care for was that the end date on a whole case of peanut butter was August 5, 2009.  I don't have much time to use a LOT of peanut butter.
The tea was fine but, when the tiny case came, I felt a bit silly for the price I had paid.

I have a feeling that this wasn't up to factory standards and was a reject batch.  I used to buy these bags at the store, and they are normally full of flavor, but these bags have almost no flavor.  I have to put two of these bags in my water to even get the green tea flavor to come out, let alone the acai berry flavor.

Anyway the food is fine - but at over one dollar a pouch - it is FAR from worth it.  Go to Walmart of the local grocery store and buy the ones for one tenth the price.
I am often disappointed with Chai teas.  This has a wonderful full bodied taste.  Love that it is caffine free.

... IF this were not at a reduced price and was eligible for free shipping, I wouldn't have even tried it. I liked that it didn't have MSG and didn't use pork as seasoning. My family is adding more vegetables to our diet as we are "eating better to live better". There was an unnatural sweet taste such that I was expecting to find Sweet Potatoes somewhere, a very unsettling feeling for me. Didn't know if this batch was inadvertantly prepared with their Sweet Potatoe product. We don't like products with hidden sugar.* (*As the commenter noted sugar IS listed in the ingredients. I should have said "unexpected sweet taste". Truthfully I was expecting similar seasoning as in Sylvia's Collard greens.)

I've never been to Sylvia's Restaurants so I don't really know if this is how it's supposed to taste. I won't order this again.

I weaned my 3 cats from a Science Diet menu that they've been on for the past 2+ years. I've been disgusted with the whole pet food debacle of late and figured that if I could treat my diet well that my cats deserved the same. The cats were not keen on the Newmans right away. In fact, they would pick through the mixture and deposit the Newmans on the floor and continue to eat only the Science Diet until I finally transitioned them over 3 weeks onto only Newmans.

The things I've noticed -- they are not eating the same quantity of food. I have a bowl that sits out all the time and so they are free to eat when they want. I add 1/2 cup increments throughout the day. They seem to enjoy the food the best when it is first put in the bowl - not wanting to eat the stuff that's been in there for 12 hours or more. I've been keeping track of their weight as I was worried about weight loss from not eating but they are all the same weight as before.

The litter habits have decreased. The two youngest cats used to use the litter box twice a day but now only once. I read on Newmans website that the digestive system can take up to 2-3 months to acclimate itself to the new diet. The only downfall for this food is the accessibility. I can easily get it at Whole Foods here in Florida if I'm in a rush (if they have it!) but when I return to my summer home in the middle of nowhere - i'll be forced to order it online. Just checked today and most places don't have it in stock now.

Other things worth mentioning - my cats never had fur balls on the Science Diet. There have been 3 fur balls in the past 4 weeks with the Newmans. Also, the cats fur tends to be a little drier than on the S.D. Other than that, i'm happy for the moment with the Newmans and have recommended it my friends.

Quick, easy, gluten free, and very, very tasty. Just the right of spice (and I used the entire spice pack) and great flavor.  Does it really taste like pad thai? Hmmm.  Well, if you've eaten pad thai in many different places you realize that there are lots of ways your typical restaurant pad thai will taste.  If you're lucky enough to live on the west coast, it'll be much better than your pad thai in the midwest, generally speaking.  Therefore this soup does resemble some pad thai's I have eaten, but it's not sweet, just mildly spicy.  Delicious!
This product was delicious and satisfying and good for you.  It made a great breakfast, especially for on the go.  And the taste and texture was awesome.

These are the best gluten free crackers I have ever tasted.  It tastes like regular crackers.  Their penne pasta is out of this world.  Although I haven't tried their cheese bites, I heard they taste like Ritz Crackers.  I highly recommend this brand.

For some reason, can't find this in stores in the Youngstown, Ohio area.  Marc's used to carry it but no longer does.  Marc's does carry other flavors of Jolly Time, but not Healthy Pop Kettle Corn.  I used to live in New Jersey and found it everywhere.  In desperation, I checked Amazon.  What DON'T they carry?  When I joined Weight Watchers many years ago, this was suggested as a low points, high fiber snack.  I love the taste.  Can't live without it.  Just hope that by the time I get to the end of the case, there aren't any freshness issues.  Love this stuff!

Excellent product.  My daughter has triplets.  One of the boys had problems with spit up.  After trying all the Similac and Enfamil products, she switched to Good Start which she had used for her older daughter.  Within days there was improvement, within about 2 weeks, his problem was gone.  All three babies are thriving on Good Start.  Price is also excellent.  The only way we get it cheaper than Amazon (with Prime) is when it is occasionally on sale.

i really like the timothy's breakfast blend and was on subscribe and save but since coffee has gone up so much have to buy at grocery store or bed bath and beyond where there are coupons. hope price comes down quick
My 3 mini dachshunds love these. Especially the youngest dog-- with his high energy level, this keeps him occupied for hours. Highly recommended to keep them 'busy'!

I adopted a rescue dog who had an allergy to corn. I checked every bag in local stores but all main fillers were corn. I thought I would have to drive to nearest pet store (120 mile round trip)to find a corn free dog food. Then I found this brand on Amazon which listed all the ingretents. No corn! My dog loves it so much, I even use it as a trick when training her. I'll be buying again and again.

Timothy's is the best coffee ever.  Smooth taste--not too weak or strong, just the right flavor.  Will continue to purchase this blend of coffee.  Also want to try other blends.  Can't go wrong with Timothy's Coffee!!
I have ordered these a couple of times and they have been fresh both times.  Delivery is quick also.  No regrets.

Summary: Very tasty, but not healthy or nutritious
Text:
Think of this as a candy/snack bar rather than a granola bar and you will not be disappointed. It's very sweet and tasty, but there's little or no nutritional value in here, despite being made from oats. The product is heavily processed and definitely what anyone would call healthy. Made with natural and artificial flavors, the ingredients list is very long (see bottom of review). It's loaded with sugar and not something you want to give yourself or your kids on a regular basis. Note how many times sugar or its variants appear in the list (glucose, fructose).

Each bar is 1.23 oz. Daily value: Fiber 1g (5%), Vitamin A (0%), Vitamin C (0%), Calcium (10%), Iron (2%). 150 calories per bar (40 from fat), 11g of sugar. I'm giving the product 4 stars based on taste and texture. It's chewy, but not hard like Nature Valley granola bars.

Ingredients: granola (whole grain rolled oats, whole grain rolled wheat, brown sugar, sunflower oil, high fructose corn syrup, dried coconut, honey, sodium bicarbonate, natural flavor, whey and whey protein concentrate), yogurt flavored coating (sugar, palm kernel and palm oil, whey protein concentrate, yogurt flavored powder, soy lecithin, natural flavor, artificial color, citric acid, salt), corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup, brown rice crisp (whole grain brown rice, sugar, malted barley flour, salt), brown sugar, glycerin, vegetable shortening (canola oil, palm and palm kernel oils), corn flakes (milled corn, sugar, salt, malted barley extract), whey mineral concentrate, oat flour, rice flour, sweetened dried strawberries (glucose syrup, strawberries, high fructose corn syrup, modified potato starch, sodium alginate), corn syrup solids, sorbitol, salt, sugar, modified food starch, soy lecithin, natural flavor, malted barley flour, sodium bicarbonate, BHT (a preservative), citric acid, water.

Made in Canada.

There were crackers cheese and chocolates but not the type in the description there were not any olives or cheese straws. Bought this specifically for the flavored and types of things because they were different terribly disappointed.

I remember when Izze was first introduced a few years back. I had it in Chicago and I immediately fell in love with it. The great packaging and the great taste made me consider it the gourmet version of sparkling water. Now they have done it again ?! it is hard to believe that anyone can make something great even better, but they did it!

The new fortified version is so refreshing that you can drink can after can and not get tired of it. My kids loved it, my girlfriend loved it, my mom loved it. This was a hit at our house. I wish that I had a chance to try the other flavors this was so good. Izze undeniably has a winner on their hands.

Summary: Run Away, Run FAR Away From This Product!
Text: I grow tired of products that claim to be healthy and the WHENEVER BARS are no exception. When you put ingredients like oatmeal, walnuts and raisins into a food, it certainly gives the illusion that you're consuming something "healthy," right? But when you look at the ingredients list and nutritional info of this OAT RAISIN WALNUT SPICE bar, the reality hits you square between the eyeballs--this is NOT good for you. Although one tiny bar contains only 100 calories, it's mostly carbohydrates that will spike your blood sugar and insulin levels. That's not very good for your body if you're attempting to eat healthy. While I suppose this product is better than most of the carbage sold in stores these days, it's not doing you any favors if you are consuming it as a means to lose weight or improve your health. Of course, if you don't care about either one of those things, then eat up. But if you want to shed pounds and ward off chronic disease, then run away, run FAR away from this product.

I bought almond flavor and wow, these are seriously the best tasting wafer snacks I've ever tasted.
I am in love. Can't wait until I try more flavors.
A very delicious berry jam.  The service was excellent.  I received it sooner than expected.  Tastes great and healthy.  A new favorite.

If you have serious food allergies or gluten intolerance, you probably bake your own (and aren't reading this review) -- but what a joy to find Dr. Lucy's cookies in Starbucks recently!  Yes, these are boxed cookies, not to be confused with homemade, which is the sterling standard for me.  But given that, they're lovely!  The body of the cookie is slightly bean-flavored, since that's what the flour blend relies on; but it's not an obtrusive flavor.  Just a bit tangy.  The milk-free chips are great:  nicely rounded flavor, not burnt or sharp.  The texture is pleasantly crisp & sandy; not tough, not hard, not chewy.  Great with coffee or tea. Our favorite is the chocolate chip variety, but the cinnamon and sugar cookies versions are delicious also.  If you're not allergic yourself, but considering buying some for guests or grandchildren who are, then I'd encourage you to go for it.  You'll find you munch on them, too, because they're just yummy, little crunchy cookies.

A great way to get this product if you like them.  I love their flavor, crunch and heat! By getting them in a bulk order, I have plenty to share. I have introduced them to several friends, who also enjoy them.

This Masa is fabulous, there is no question about it. Thank you.
Please be careful though with your packaging. One pack was broken, so 1/3 of the Masa was lost in the middle of the packaging!

Wow! FINALLY there is an AWESOME gluten-free pasta. I am in heaven! They are worth every penny. I've tried their fettucine, penne, and spaghetti pasta so far... and enjoyed them all. I just ordered more from Amazon. Although the other rice and potato pastas out there are tolerable, they just don't have the right taste and texture... so I had slowly given up on eating pasta. Now I am in love with pasta again! Thank you, Le Veneziane!
This maple sugar is greeeeat!  Use less maple sugar that you would white or other sugars.  I put it on oatmeal with brown sugar, and i put some on roasted sweet potatoes! amazing!

Summary: Only a pack of three! And tastes terrible!
Text: This was on super discount when I got it so it was only a waste of like $3 but nowhere does it say that it's actually some super disgusting, highly potent mutant cousin of Earl Grey tea. I bought it thinking it was straight black Ceylon tea. No such luck and now I have nothing to make fermented kombucha with. Utter disappointment and I love Earl Grey!

I had purchased this ginger once in the past, and it was very good quality. However, the latest order that I made gave me quite a shock! The ginger powder had a very peculiar, chemical odor. I tasted a small sample and had to rinse my mouth as it was disgusting. Then I looked more closely at the label, and discovered the problem. This ginger is from China, and although labeled as organic, I'm quite sure that it was laced with pesticide or other chemicals. I have read reports of "organic" ginger leaving China literally covered with insecticide powder, and I suspect that this is what may have happened to this batch. I would recommend that you avoid this product until these issues are resolved.
What you see in the picture is EXACTLY what you get. All the snacks are equivalent to what is in the picture, everything under them is packing peanuts and paper. Horrible disappointing.
The best bargain around. I searched all over to find this product with a variety and it allowed me to try all 6 flavors at a great price and free shipping!

The Almond Trail Mix bars aren't exactly what I expected but they are still pretty tasty. Extremely dense and chewy, they're definitely a filling snack. However, it has a lot of calories for such a little package if that's something you care about ... I was hoping for a slightly bigger bar to share with my wife but it's not really large enough to split. The trail mix flavor is *definitely* the prevalent flavor here instead of almond, which was also a little bit disappointing since I love almonds.

Minor quibbles aside, this is a tasty and healthy snack item. I'd order it again if it went on sale.

This is my favorite flavor of Kind bars. Since it doesn't have that much fruit the carbs are lower (9 net) which is what I'm looking for. It is extremely crunchy, not chewy, but has great flavor. It definitely holds you over between meals. Good stuff!

I was surprised to discover that the salt is packaged while damp. I don't know what accounts for the dampness, but it causes the salt crystals to be a bit sticky, which hinders the electric salt grinder that I'm using. I have not had this problem with other brands of salt. Anyway, I was going to return it, but instead chose to spread the salt on some wax paper on a cookie tray and let in bake in the oven for 1/2 hour, which removed the moisture and now it seems fine! One really shouldn't have to do that, right? Anyway, I won't be ordering this product again because of the dampness, but this may not be a problem for others and I must say that the salt does taste great.

My cat is 13 years old.  I had been feeding her Friskies Dental Diet for most of her adult life, but it was discontinued.  While on the dental diet she never needed to have her teeth cleaned.  I decided to try the Science Diet brand.  She seems to really enjoy the taste of it.  I mix it with some smaller dry food and she picks out the large Science Diet food first. Like many others, I am trying to give up sodas and drink more water. In the past I have used the crystal light drink add-ins with mixed results, so when I saw this product I wanted to give it a try. I like the concept of the liquid flavoring, that would eliminate the problem of the powders not dissolving all the way. In addition, the bottle would allow the user to add as little or as much of the flavoring as he/she would like, for a customized beverage.

With all of that in mind, I had high hopes for this product, and I was excited to try it out. Unfortunately, my hopes were dashed once I actually used the product. First, the bottle states to use "two drops" of flavoring for a 16 oz bottle of water. I did use two drops, and aside from making a slight change in the color of the water, there was no change to the flavor of the water. I took another bottle of water and added two "squirts" of flavoring to the water, and the results were more dramatic. I must first add that fortunately for me, I did not experience the "chemically" or "bleach" smell that others seem to have experienced with this product. What I did smell was the strong smell of "artificial" peach scent. The scent immediately reminded me of a peach candle - that is to say very strong and artificial. Despite the smell, I started to drink and while the flavor of the drink (while drinking it) wasn't too bad, it did leave an aftertaste in my mouth that I did not care for. Also, bringing the bottle to my mouth caused my nose to be assaulted by the fake-peach smell again. Try as I might, I was not able to finish that bottle.

In order to provide an accurate appraisal of the product, I experimented more with the flavoring, slowly adding more drops (but less than the two squirts) until a more acceptable scent was acheived. The first thing I determined is that there is no way to acheive as many bottles of flavored water as the package states. Most people would have to use twice as much (at the minimum) to get any kind of flavor at all, which greatly reduces the amount of water you can flavor from one bottle. Unfortunately, even with less flavoring, there was still a lingering after-taste. I have talked with friends of mine who like the MIO products, and they have suggested that maybe it is the "tea" part of the flavoring that is leaving the after-taste, as they have not had that problem with other flavors of the product.

Overall, I am disappointed that this product did not live up to my expectaions. Although I know of people who use and like this flavoring, I am not sure I will be purchasing any additional flavors. The cost of this item in grocery stores is somewhat high, and I am hesitant to purchase a 4-pk from Amazon in the event that I won't use them. The overpowering smell, as well as the after-taste from the flavoring has led me to determine that I will be best served by continuing to use crystal light.

UPDATE*******
While my rating of the peach tea remains the same, armed with a high value coupon I did purchase another flavor of MIO - this time the strawberry-watermelon flavor, and I was very pleased with the results. I will be posting a review for that item later.
